sentences.speaker: interviewer
sentences.text: Thanks for sitting down with us. Can you start by telling us why you decided to run?

sentences.speaker: dana
sentences.text: Um, sure. So, the short version is, sorry, let me start that again.

sentences.speaker: dana
sentences.text: I decided to run because I kept going to council meetings and leaving with more questions than answers.

sentences.speaker: dana
sentences.text: I've lived in Ward 3 for nineteen years, and I run a small bakery on Elm Street.

sentences.speaker: dana
sentences.text: Over the last few years I've watched neighbors struggle with rising costs while the city couldn't explain where the money was going.

sentences.speaker: dana
sentences.text: At some point you stop complaining and you step up.

sentences.speaker: interviewer
sentences.text: Property taxes have been a big issue this year. What's your view?

sentences.speaker: dana
sentences.text: We've seen taxes increase while residents are asking where the money is going.

sentences.speaker: dana
sentences.text: Our assessment went up again this spring, and nobody on my street could tell you what changed.

sentences.speaker: dana
sentences.text: I'm not against paying for good services. I'm against paying more without a clear account of it.

sentences.speaker: dana
sentences.text: So my first priority would be a plain-language budget that every household can actually read.

sentences.speaker: dana
sentences.text: Uh, the the budget, I mean, the whole thing, it's just, yeah.

sentences.speaker: interviewer
sentences.text: What would you actually change in the first year?

sentences.speaker: dana
sentences.text: Three things.

sentences.speaker: dana
sentences.text: First, publish every contract over fifty thousand dollars online, within a week of signing.

sentences.speaker: dana
sentences.text: Second, hold two evening budget sessions in the ward, not just one daytime meeting downtown.

sentences.speaker: dana
sentences.text: Third, set up a simple tracker for road and sidewalk repairs, so people can see when their request will be handled.

sentences.speaker: dana
sentences.text: None of that is expensive. It's mostly about deciding to do it.

sentences.speaker: interviewer
sentences.text: Your opponent says those ideas are nice but unrealistic. How do you respond?

sentences.speaker: dana
sentences.text: I'd say other cities our size already do it.

sentences.speaker: dana
sentences.text: Look, I think, I think transparency is, it's important, you know.

sentences.speaker: dana
sentences.text: Riverside publishes its contracts, and their council says it actually reduced complaints.

sentences.speaker: dana
sentences.text: It's not unrealistic. It's just unfamiliar here.

sentences.speaker: interviewer
sentences.text: And going back to taxes for a moment, anything to add?

sentences.speaker: dana
sentences.text: Just that taxes keep rising and people want to know where the money goes.

sentences.speaker: dana
sentences.text: Like I said before, it's about being able to see it.

sentences.speaker: interviewer
sentences.text: Last question. What do you want voters to remember about you?

sentences.speaker: dana
sentences.text: That I'll answer the phone.

sentences.speaker: dana
sentences.text: If you call my office, you'll get a person, and you'll get a straight answer, even if it's not the one you wanted.

sentences.speaker: dana
sentences.text: That's the job.
